title: Console walkthrough — usage analytics & per-route cost breakdown
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Trident Logistics through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for latency-sensitive routing and has compliance questions around KMS and audit logs. Next steps: send pricing, share security docs, schedule POC kickoff/benchmarking.
next_steps: Maya: Share Dedicated + Hosted pricing spreadsheet (2026-03-06)
Liam: Schedule POC kickoff and benchmark window with Trident (week of 3/16)
Maya: Send SOC2 + security summary + KMS integration doc (link)
action_items: Maya Chen - Send pricing and config options by 2026-03-06
Liam Ortiz - Setup POC infra checklist & benchmark plan by 2026-03-10
Priya Raman - Share sample traffic patterns and top 10 routes by 2026-03-09
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Liam our solutions engineer is here too.
[00:07] Priya Raman: Hi, thanks. excited to see the console walkthrough, we've been looking at per-route costs and wondering how predictable inference spend will be.
[00:15] Liam Ortiz: Great, we'll jump right in. Quick agenda: usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, and routing/fallbacks. We'll keep it practical.
[00:28] Ethan Cole: Quick ask up front — latency is our top priority for customer-facing routes. Cost is important but latency-first for two routes.
[00:35] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll highlight how you can pin routes to Dedicated pools and monitor SLOs per route.
[00:43] [00:45] Liam Ortiz: (screen share) Ok console home, usage overview — you can see token-level consumption by model family, and we have a breakdown by route. This is live data sampled at one minute intervals, so it aligns pretty closely with what you'll see in production.
[01:05] Samir Patel: The token-level thing — does that include system tokens and tool calls? sometimes we send structured tool calls.
[01:12] Liam Ortiz: Good question. We currently attribute system vs user tokens; tool-calls show up under the integrations column. Sometimes the transcriber flips the labels, you'll see ist sometimes 'Redwood Dedicate' spelled wrong in the logs but the data is intact.
[01:28] Priya Raman: That's fine. show the route-level dashboard.
[01:32] Liam Ortiz: Sure. Here is a per-route view — each route is a logical endpoint you register. On the left you get request rate, p50/p95 latency, token cost per response, and error rate. There's a cost column that maps to our per-token pricing and any overhead for dedicated pools.
[01:50] [02:00] Liam Ortiz: If you click into a route you get a time-series of cost per minute, top prompts driving tokens, and an estimate of monthly spend extrapolated from the selected window. You can change time granularity 1m/5m/1h.
[02:20] Ethan Cole: How accurate is the extrapolated monthly spend? in our traffic thing we have big spikes during EOD batch jobs.
[02:27] Maya Chen: The console lets you select 'exclude scheduled batch windows' or apply a percentile (p90) for projection. For spikes you can also see the peak contributors so you can decide to route batch jobs to cheaper variants or schedule offline.
[02:44] Samir Patel: Can we map routes to specific GPU pools? like route A uses Dedicated g4/rtx, route B goes hosted cheaper model.
[02:52] Liam Ortiz: Yup. Routing policies: latency-first routes can pin to Dedicated pools with autoscale policies. Cheaper routes can fallback to hosted open-model variants. We demo the fallback below.
[03:05] [03:15] Liam Ortiz: Switching to cost-breakdown view — token costs, infra (GPU-hours), and egress. We show cost per thousand tokens and you can toggle quantization savings applied by our Optimize module.
[03:32] Priya Raman: Quantization — what model fidelity loss are we looking at? we can't have hallucination increases.
[03:39] Liam Ortiz: Typical LLMs lose minimal NLU accuracy on 4-bit quant when prompts are short, but we recommend running evals. Our Optimize suggests quant profiles per route based on your prompts. We can run a blind A/B during the POC.
[03:55] [04:00] Ethan Cole: Security — we need KMS + audit logs and SSO integration.
[04:05] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We have KMS/HSM options for Private and Dedicated, audit logs in the Console with retention settings, and SAML/SSO + RBAC. I'll share the security packet after the call.
[04:20] Priya Raman: Are there SOC2 or ISO docs?
[04:23] Maya Chen: Yes SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs. Link coming. (note: often transcriptions will mangle acronyms, sometimes shows as 'S O C two')
[04:34] [04:45] Liam Ortiz: Back to the route config — you can define traffic weights, canary policies, and fallback chains. For example if Dedicated pool is saturated we can spillover to a cheaper hosted variant or to a smaller context length model to preserve latency.
[05:03] Samir Patel: How do you measure per-route token caching? we have prefixes common to many requests.
[05:10] Liam Ortiz: We surface hit-rate for KV/prefix caching per route. If you have high reuse across sessions we can show potential token savings and suggest cache TTL adjustments.
[05:25] [05:35] Priya Raman: Show the alerting. we want to be paged if p95 goes above X ms or cost exceeds Y.
[05:42] Liam Ortiz: Alerts tie to any metric in the dashboard. You can push to Slack/PagerDuty and define composite alerts across routes.
[05:55] [06:00] Ethan Cole: On pricing: our CFO wants a simple number for 3 routes high-priority. Do you provide an estimated committed pricing for Dedicated?
[06:08] Maya Chen: We do reserved capacity pricing with monthly/annual commits. I'll send a pricing example sheet — it includes burst options and SLA tiers. For the demo we can put down rough numbers.
[06:20] Priya Raman: Any benchmarking we should run? token throughput, p95 under load?
[06:26] Liam Ortiz: We recommend a synthetic run and a replay of a day of your traffic. We'll instrument with tracing hooks and collect p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens. For throughput we can run continuous batching profiles to see tradeoffs between latency and cost.
[06:44] [07:05] Samir Patel: Network — VPC peering or Private deployment needed for our data residency.
[07:12] Maya Chen: For high-regulated workloads we offer Private deployments (customer-controlled VPC) or Dedicated with VPC peering and private connectivity. KMS keys stay in your account for Private.
[07:25] Priya Raman: If we do Private on-prem — how much ops from our side?
[07:30] Liam Ortiz: We provide an on-prem package with an installer and support; baseline infra and a runbook. It's heavier ops but gives full control. For most, Dedicated with VPC peering hits the requirements.
[07:45] [08:00] Liam Ortiz: Quick demo of a scenario: route A is our customer chat, pinned to Dedicated. Under load we see p95 climb — console suggests two steps: increase min replicas for that pool, and enable KV prewarm. You can apply both from the UI.
[08:20] Priya Raman: Nice. the UI change — any API for infra-as-code? we prefer terraform.
[08:26] Maya Chen: Yes we have Terraform provider and an API for programmatic config. We'll share examples.
[08:35] [08:45] Ethan Cole: Competitor question — if we go with ManagedCloudAI, cost looks lower for similar latency. Why Redwood?
[08:52] Maya Chen: A few reasons — we focus on predictable inference economics and observability per route. Our console ties rollouts, tracing, and cost metrics together and supports private deployments with KMS. Also our Optimize module recommends quant profiles and batching settings tailored to routes.
[09:10] Liam Ortiz: Also our fallbacks and model catalog are tuned for graceful degradation. If a high latency event occurs you can route automatically to a compatible lower-cost model.
[09:25] [09:40] Samir Patel: Any gotchas on token accounting? sometimes third-party transcribers split tokens and we end up double counting.
[09:48] Liam Ortiz: We attribute at request boundary; integrations/third-party wrappers sometimes re-encode — we'll work together to confirm via sample logs during the POC.
[10:02] [10:15] Priya Raman: Let's talk POC sizing — we want two weeks, simulate our peak day, and run quant A/B.
[10:22] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Proposed POC: 2-week bench, replay peak day, test p95 under 100ms for high-priority routes, run quant A/B for medium routes. Liam will send a checklist.
[10:40] Liam Ortiz: I'll attach a benchmark checklist and a sample replay script. expect to iterate on model choices — sometimes a smaller context length + caching gives better tail latency than a larger model.
[11:02] [11:15] Ethan Cole: Any SLA credits if dedicated pool misses target?
[11:20] Maya Chen: Yes, for Dedicated we provide SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; fallback policies also reduce impact. We'll include SLA details in the pricing doc.
[11:35] [11:45] Priya Raman: Can you show a sample bill-back report? our finance requires per-biz-unit chargeback.
[11:52] Liam Ortiz: The Console can export per-route cost CSVs and map them to tags for chargeback. You can integrate with billing exports to your warehouse.
[12:10] Samir Patel: Are audit logs tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody for some events.
[12:16] Maya Chen: Audit logs are immutable in the control plane; for Private we can ship logs into your account S3 and sign them with KMS. We'll detail chain-of-custody options.
[12:33] [12:45] Priya Raman: Good. any other quick wins?
[12:48] Liam Ortiz: Optimize suggests batching and quant profiles per route. Often turning on prefix caching for session-heavy routes drops token spend 20-40%.
[13:05] [13:15] Ethan Cole: Ok let's recap next steps.
[13:18] Maya Chen: Recap: I'll send pricing and security docs; Liam will send POC checklist and schedule; Priya will share traffic samples and top routes. We'll aim to kick off the POC week of Mar 16.
[13:35] Priya Raman: Thanks, appreciate the walkthrough.
[13:38] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with links to the docs and the pricing sheet.
[13:46] [END]
